A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Reason to Rote: Rethinking Memorization in Reasoning. All 21 pages in each version, including figures, equations, references, and Appendices A–I, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer experiments on four-digit addition and two-hop relational reasoning, including learning curves, probing, causal interventions, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix model-size, noise-rate, and Qwen2.5-0.5B experiments.

M1.justification: The Transformer architectures and language-modeling objective are unchanged. The probing, EAP circuit discovery, INLP, and activation-patching procedures are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic four-digit addition and two-hop relational reasoning tasks, with the same clean and noisy-label scenarios. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons are unchanged, including Random and Mean Probe in Figure 4c and the random-patching controls in Figure 6b. The newly cited works are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain the FDA 40,000/10,000 and THR 6,400/1,600 training/validation splits. Noise rates, model configurations, training budgets, first-answer-token evaluation, probing splits, and metrics also match.

E4.justification: The circuit-overlap, bridge-entity, attention-head, and neuron-patching analyses are unchanged. Appendix model-size and noise-rate comparisons, first-token analyses, and additional outlier-heuristic examples are all retained.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same statistical reporting practices, without reported repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty reporting is added or removed.

E6.justification: The original numerical results, curves, and qualitative findings in Figures 3–14 match. For example, both report the same neuron-activation shift from 2.07 to 0.18 in Figure 6a; the appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The faithfulness definitions in Equations 1–2 and the mathematical descriptions of EAP and INLP are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: noise memorization builds on reasoning mechanisms, uses distributed encodings, and operates through outlier heuristics in FDA.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly cautions that verbatim completion need not establish training-set membership, citing Liu et al. (2025). This adds a specific qualification about interpreting memorization evidence; interpretations of the paper's own experiments and its stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, data-generation instructions, hyperparameters, and implementation disclosures are unchanged. Appendix H retains the same Python, PyTorch, Transformers, and NVIDIA A100 80GB information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al. (2025) on limitations of completion-based memorization tests, plus Mondorf et al. (2025) and Bertolazzi et al. (2025) as support for synthetic-data studies. The existing novelty positioning and comparison with Huang et al. (2024) remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a first-author research-visit/current-affiliation footnote, inserts the related-work caution, and briefly rewrites the synthetic-data paragraph in Section 6. The section order and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added footnote and literature material cause limited column and page reflow: Discussion begins on page 9 instead of page 8, and Acknowledgements on page 10 instead of page 9. All 14 figures retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: The new Section 5 caution adds useful nuance about what verbatim completion can establish, while Section 6 gains relevant literature context. These modestly improve the framing; the original experiments, appendix evidence, central conclusions, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
